subject: Affordability runway & pilot gating — token economics, batching/caching levers
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moore <alex@platinumpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Affordability runway & pilot gating — token economics, batching/caching levers

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and a clear set of next steps.

TL;DR: Primary affordability blocker is token run-rate for external-facing fraud checks (high QPS, short context). We discussed a 6–12 week pilot to validate quality/lower-cost paths: 1) batching + KV-prefix caching for session-heavy flows, 2) quantized model variant for non-realtime backfills, 3) fixed monthly reserved capacity for predictable unit cost.

Pain points you shared:
- 20–25M inference tokens/month for risk scoring peak days — current infra cost is high and unpredictable.
- SLA need: sub-200ms P50 on lookup + score path (10–30ms optional for early reject).
- Compliance: no PII persisted outside the VPC; audit logs required for production runs.

Goals we agreed on:
- Demonstrate a 40–60% reduction in per-token billable cost inside the pilot window while meeting score accuracy thresholds (AUC delta < 1.5% vs baseline).
- Validate a routing policy that pushes matchable prefixes to cache/batching while keeping worst-case latency within SLA.
- Produce a simple TCO model comparing burst-on-demand vs reserved capacity + batching.

Proposed pilot scope (minimal viable):
- 3-week integration sprint (ingest sample traffic, enable prefix KV caching, perf test)
- 6-week observation window with A/B on quantized variant for non-critical traffic
- Deliverables: cost-runway spreadsheet, per-route latency/cost dashboard, quality regression report, SOW for production rollout if pilot meets targets.

Attached: draft SOW and cost anchors workbook (redwood_pilot_sow_draft.pdf, cost-runway-anchors.xlsx).

Open questions / asks from PlatinumPay:
1) Can Procurement share a target monthly cap for the pilot (if you have a ceiling that helps us size dedicated capacity)?
2) Do you have an internal list of high-frequency prefixes (example: login/email-normalized) we can seed into cache to accelerate savings?
3) Any preferred encryption/KMS requirements for the VPC/private deployment?

Next steps I propose:
- You share the pilot budget cap and a small sample trace (anonymized) — target by Thu 4/16.
- We schedule a 45-min engineering alignment with your SREs to walk infra requirements next week.
- We finalize the SOW and return a signed DocuSign by EOW if budget aligns.

If that matches your take, I’ll get the HubSpot deal updated and loop Ops for scheduling.

Thanks —
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_pilot_sow_draft.pdf (PDF, 58KB), cost-runway-anchors.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)

From: Alex Moore <alex@platinumpay.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@platinumpay.com>, SRE Team <ops@platinumpay.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Affordability runway & pilot gating — token economics, batching/caching levers

Thanks Priyom — solid recap. A few clarifications from our side: we can commit to a pilot cap of $60k for month 1 (engineering + infra) assuming the savings trajectory is visible within the observation window.

Answers/notes:
- We will provide an anonymized 7-day sample trace (no PII) by Thu 4/16 EOD. Ops will include traffic labeled by route so you can identify hot prefixes.
- KMS: we use AWS KMS with single-tenant keys; we need Redwood to support encrypt-at-rest with customer-managed keys for the pilot.
- For the SLA: can we tolerate occasional cold-cache misses that spike a small percentage of requests beyond 200ms (we can live with P95 up to 500ms for <1% of traffic)?

Procurement — copying you to see the SOW and confirm if $60k cap is acceptable or whether you need an internal PO before signature.

Alex
Head of Product — PlatinumPay

On Tue, Apr 14, 2026 at 3:03 PM Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick written recap so we have alignment and a clear set of next steps.
>

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Affordability runway & pilot gating — ops notes

Looping in a couple quick ops notes based on Priyom/Alex thread:
- We should pre-seed the KV cache with the top ~500 prefixes from their 7-day sample; that should recover a large portion of hot tokens and reduce billable token count quickly.
- Suggest we use a conservative batching window (5–10ms) for the realtime path and enable a larger batching fallback (50–150ms) for backfill/async scoring to maximize throughput.
- For KMS: our private deployment supports CMK; I'll draft the KMS attachment requirements for the SOW.

Marissa — can you start a simplified TCO worksheet that compares: on-demand GPU vs 1-month reserved pool at 50% utilization with caching enabled? I’ll put rough perf numbers in table.

Karthik
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Moore <alex@platinumpay.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@platinumpay.com>
Date: Fri, 16 Apr 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Affordability runway & pilot gating — token economics, batching/caching levers (confirming next steps)

Alex / team — thanks for the quick responses and for committing a pilot cap. Confirming next steps and owners so there’s no ambiguity:

1) PlatinumPay: share anonymized 7-day sample trace + list of top prefixes (due Thu 4/16 EOD) — owner: Alex / Ops.
2) Redwood: update SOW with KMS appendix and conservative TCO variant, return via DocuSign for signature — owner: Priyom (deliver Tue 4/20).
3) Redwood Ops: pre-seed KV cache demo plan + batching windows proposed for realtime/backfill — owner: Karthik (deliver draft infra runbook Mon 4/20).
4) Procurement: confirm whether a PO is required prior to signature or if DocuSign signature is sufficient under the $60k cap — owner: Procurement (PlatinumPay).

If we get the trace on Thu we can hit the integration sprint next Monday and have meaningful cost signals in 3 weeks.

If that sounds good I’ll create the HubSpot activity and schedule the 45-min engineering alignment for Mon 4/20 (calendar invite to follow).

Thanks —
Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_pilot_sow_draft.pdf (PDF, 58KB), cost-runway-anchors.xlsx (XLSX, 120KB)
